To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ramsey-Boi-teux approach to public goods is equivalent to Bayesian mechanism design if and only if it satisfies renegotiation proofness, and that the Ramsey- Boiteux approach to public and private goods is equivalent to mixed bundling if it does not satisfy renegotiation proofness.

(i) the Ramsey-Boitieux approach is not equivalent to Bayesian mechanism design; (ii) it is superior only under a strong assumption of renegotiation proof equilibrium; (iii) it is inferior to Bayesian mechanism design in general.

the Ramsey-Boîteux approach to the design of optimal excludable public-good provision and pricing is equivalent to the Bayesian approach if and only if the optimal mechanism satisfies renegotiation proofness, and that, without this property, the optimal mechanism is one involving mixed bundling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to design optimal pricing schemes when consumers have heterogeneous tastes for the public good.
the question of whether the Ramsey-Boîteux approach to optimal taxation and pricing can be extended to the case of excludable private goods.
the relation between two different approaches to the provision and price of excludable goods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ramsey-Boîteux approach is the right way to go, but only if it is supplemented by a mechanism involving a mixed bundling of private and public goods.

, for the problem of the provision and pricing excludable public good, the Ramsey-Boitexu approach and the Bayesian mechanism design approach are equivalent if and only it is not possible to improve the mechanism by adding mixed bundling.
, in the presence of private information, Ramsey-Boiteaux pricing is a special case of mixed bundling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ramsey-Boiteaux pricing and bundling are equivalent under the condition of renegotiation-proofness, and that the latter approach is superior otherwise.
Ramsey-Boiteaux pricing can only be implemented as a Bayesian mechanism if the planner has no bargaining power.
the Ramsey-Boîteux approach to pricing is equivalent to the revelation approach if and only if the public good is a pure public good and there are no indivisibilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ramsey-Boitex approach to the provision of excludable goods should be extended to include a mechanism design element.
the standard Ramsey-Boiteuux approach to the pricing of excludabe public goods, although widely used, is incomplete.

, in the context of the provision of excludable goods, Ramsey-Boiteaux pricing is only a second-best approach, which is inferior to mixed bundling if the government can commit to a fixed allocation of private goods.
